items.raw_snippet: # Firmus valuation approaches $7b in fresh Nvidia investment. Artificial intelligence infrastructure start-up Firmus is expected to be valued at nearly $7 billion after the world’s biggest company Nvidia doubled its investment in what’s slated to be its final capital raising as a private company. Firmus was scrambling to finalise the third and final tranche of its whopper $1 billion-plus pre-IPO raising on Monday night, according to those close to the company who were not authorised to speak publicly. It includes a share sale to Nvidia and other strategic investors, and comes hours before its management make their maiden pitch to potential IPO investors in Asia on Tuesday. items.title: AI巨头Anthropic携4亿美元进军生命科学
items.snippet: Claude开发商Anthropic投资4亿美元押注生物医药领域，拓展AI在生命科学的应用场景。
items.raw_snippet: # AI Giant Anthropic Leans Into Life Sciences With $400M Coefficient Bio Catch. ## Anthropic in October last year iterated its Claude AI model to better cater to biopharma purposes. AI leader Anthropic is pushing further into the life sciences space by acquiring the New York–based startup Coefficient Bio for around $400 million. The source also didn’t specify what Coefficient brings to the table and how the acquisition will enrich Anthropic’s AI operations in the life sciences. In October 2025, the AI giant launched Claude Life Sciences, an iteration of its machine learning model specifically designed to help professionals across the biopharma industry, covering scientists, clinical trial coordinators and regulatory managers. 3d illustration of a robotic hand holding a medical capsule on blue backdrop with space for text and images. AI has also helped reinvigorate biopharma’s IPO market, according to experts interviewed by *BioSpace*, who noted that startups can use advanced algorithms to better make their case to investors, who in turn can use these models to better assess their risk.

items.snippet: As firms adopt these technologies to increase efficiency, enhance insights, and ...
items.raw_snippet: As firms adopt these technologies to increase efficiency, enhance insights, and accelerate deal execution, a critical question arises: **Is AI replacing human investment bankers, or is it transforming their roles entirely?**. Despite the undeniable power of AI to transform workflows, there are several aspects of investment banking where human skills remain essential. As AI automates many traditional analyst tasks, the role of investment banking professionals, especially early‑career analysts, is shifting toward higher‑value responsibilities. An investment banking course that incorporates modern tools and teaches students to work with AI accelerates this transition and prepares learners for future‑ready roles. As investment banking evolves, the narrative that AI will fully replace human bankers is oversimplified. By pursuing structured learning, such as an investment banking course that combines finance fundamentals with exposure to modern tools, aspiring professionals can position themselves for success in a landscape where human intelligence and artificial intelligence work together synergistically. The increasing use of data analytics, artificial intelligence (AI), and machine learning has transformed how people and institutions make investment decisions.

items.raw_snippet: When most people think about AI in go-to-market contexts, they usually start with customer data. But in practice, the useful enterprise data layer is much broader than that. Even if the enterprise data layer is strong, AI still needs to know what the company actually sells, how those offerings fit together, how they should be described, where they apply, and what guidance should shape customer-facing actions. That is why I increasingly think of product marketing, product management, product design, and related roles as stewards of a shared intelligence layer, not just owners of messaging or launch materials. They are helping define the commercial truth that AI will draw from inside marketing, sales, customer success, and other revenue workflows. Enterprise data cannot be owned in a way that disconnects it from the workflows of marketing, sales, and customer success.
